topThreeProblems: Wrong legal guidance on the product's own showcase question. explain_rule (topics itar-us-person and laa-non-citizen) tells users that green-card holders 'don't need that stricter rule' and that the LAA pathway 'is for someone who does NOT qualify as a U.S. person at all.' The cited source says the opposite: 32 CFR 117.10(k), which I fetched from the eCFR API, is headed 'Non-U.S. citizens', so LPRs fall under it. Clearance eligibility requires U.S. citizenship. The errors compound downstream. get_role_rubric for Fury role 1615aeb4… (its posting says 'Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance') asks only 'are you a U.S. person (citizen, green card holder…)?'. The homepage hero transcript answers 'Yes' to 'can a green card holder work the Anduril Fury role?'. /try shows a 'Likely US-person required' chip on a TS/Secret role. A green-card holder following this would be steered toward roles they almost certainly cannot clear for.

The PII/CUI guard is much weaker than the privacy page says, and parts of the MCP surface skip it entirely. I sent 92 payloads through prepare_consented_card.notes, and MCP and POST /api/tools/* gave identical results for all 92. Of the 80 payloads in categories the privacy page says it refuses, 38 were accepted and echoed verbatim into the card. Accepted items include: every CUI marking I tried ('CUI//SP-EXPT', 'CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION', FOUO, Distribution Statement D, the AECA export warning); 'described' and homoglyph SECRET//NOFORN; A-number 'A-123-456-789', driver's license, EDIPI/CAC, I-94; and clearance-record text such as 'An incident report was filed in DISS on 2025-01-03 for a security violation'. Also accepted were SSN variants ('536/22/8790', Arabic-Indic digits, a line break inside the number, spaced digits, '536-22-8790') and DOB forms like 'b. 3/14/88' and 'birthdate 19880314'. MCP prompts/get (check_my_eligibility, prep_for_role, share_intro_card) is not guarded at all: it echoed role_id='536-22-8790', an email, and 'DISS record: … SSN 536-22-8790' into the returned prompt text. JSON key names are never scanned: an SSN used as a key comes back in 'Unrecognized key: "123-45-6789"'. Tool-not-found and resource-not-found errors (MCP and REST) echo SSNs too. All of this contradicts the claim that 'every tool call is scanned before anything else happens — before validation'.

The opt-in, anonymity, and 'no free text' promises are weaker than stated. (1) contribute_anonymous_signal writes to a persistent pool but is annotated readOnlyHint:true, so clients that auto-approve read-only tools may never ask the user. That undercuts the 'explicitly agreed' opt-in. (2) get_aggregated_signal discloses exact counts below the k-floor (1 for the Fury role, 3 for Anduril, 2 for Saronic, 1 for Hadrian). Contributions carry no identity, and a 25-request burst got no rate limiting. So the 'at least 5 people' floor is really '5 calls', which padding and before/after differencing can defeat. This is inferred from design; I did not pad the live pool. (3) prepare_signed_attestation is advertised as 'no free text', yet it accepted a validly signed payload with a hidden 'holder':'Jane Q. Public, 1600 Pennsylvania Ave NW' field. That name and address ended up in credential.proof.signedPayload, while the human-readable shareableMarkdown showed only the two enum claims. A 2099 issued_at was also accepted, despite the claim that the signature 'proves… WHEN'. (4) prepare_consented_card put age, race, sex, disability, religion, pregnancy and 'from Iran' into an employer-facing card with no warning. The README also overclaims that the server 'never receives… PII, clearance details'.

function.evidence:
Mechanics are excellent. The official @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32 StreamableHTTPClientTransport connected in 332 ms and listed 16 tools, 4 prompts and 3 resources. Every tool returned schema-valid structuredContent, and every result carried sources[] plus a disclaimer. The 92-payload battery matched exactly between MCP and the /try REST API. Latency: p50 103 ms, p95 147 ms. Input validation is strict: an unknown role_id is rejected, and the aggregate tool enforces 'exactly one of role_id/company_slug'. The DCSA headline figures are correct. I rendered page 61 of the cited NISPPAC 2026-09-02 slides and they match exactly: Secret 21+59+117=197, TS 20+97+126=243, prior Secret quarters 180/209/183, TS investigation 234 to 97, adjudication 40 to 126.

Content correctness has real defects:
(1) The green-card/LAA error described in the top problems, which also breaks the Fury rubric.
(2) Evidence labeled 'stated' and 'verbatim' is cut off at the 'U.S.' abbreviation: 'Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.', 'security clearance.', 'protected individual as defined by 8 U.'
(3) estimate_timeline returns 180–270 days for lapsed_gt_2y identically for secret, ts and ts_sci. The cited slide shows TS at 221–333 across the same quarters. Secret lapsed>2y with no FCL gives 270–540, while a new Secret initial with no FCL gives 287–467. The uncertaintyNote calls the figures 'medians' while a driver says no median exists. dcsa-timeliness quotes the PAC QPR as '61 days' Secret-tier for FY26-Q3, but the QPR table shows 57; 61 is the Q2 value.
(4) run_job_preview gives a Senior Manufacturing Engineer a 'telemetry ingest fix' standup and 'learn the codebase'.
(5) Searching 'ITAR' or 'polygraph' returns 0 roles.

trueUserValue.evidence:
Genuine value: live speedrun-network roles with requirement signals labeled stated or inferred (search_defense_roles over 200 postings, filtered by clearance level). Correctly sourced, current DCSA timeliness data with an honest single-figure-versus-range explanation. A useful NBIS/DISS-JVS 2026 transition explainer. get_company_profile honestly returns gaps instead of fit claims.

The central use case is undermined. A green-card holder asking about a Secret-clearance role is told, in effect, that they are eligible. That is worse than a plain search of DCSA or 32 CFR 117.10, or a general-purpose LLM, which usually gets 'clearances require citizenship' right.

The prep tools are mostly string templating. Interview questions read 'Tell me about a time your work connected to: "Bachelors Degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, or Manufacturing Engineering"' and '…"10+ years of experience…"'. The trial 'brief' lists three quoted responsibilities but never defines an actual task, and the rubric bands only restate each quote. Job-preview scenes are role-agnostic. A capable agent could produce the same or better from the posting alone, so the differentiated value is concentrated in role search and the sourced timeline and rule data.

aestheticsUx.evidence:
I ran axe-core 4.14 (WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 A and AA plus best-practice) on /, /try, /privacy and /sources, each in light and dark at 1280 px and 375 px: 0 violations in all 16 combinations, no horizontal overflow, page loads 0.63–1.03 s. The skip link is the first Tab stop. The Radix tabs move focus and selection with the arrow keys and show a 2px :focus-visible ring. The FAQ accordion sets aria-expanded and reveals its answer. A guard rejection in /try appears as a calm role=alert panel ('We can't process that here' plus the reason and an 'Edit and try again' button), and the user's input is preserved. Typography and hierarchy are restrained and consistent, and dark mode is solid.

Weaknesses: the 16-tab strip truncates at 1280 px ('Consented card' is cut off and later tools are hidden behind horizontal scroll). Posting chips are ellipsized ('Anduril Industries pos…'). The mobile filter select is clipped ('Any clearanc'). The homepage's animated example transcript models a legally wrong answer. I can't name a concrete reason it beats the best comparable product, so it doesn't reach 9.

trustPrivacyCompliance.evidence:
Strengths: strict CSP (connect-src 'self', frame-ancestors 'none'), HSTS preload, no cookies, and zero third-party requests from /try (Playwright request log). The privacy page's worked SSN example reproduces exactly (HTTP 400 pii_cui_rejected) on REST and MCP. The guard catches the canonical forms: dashed, spaced or dotted SSNs, fullwidth and zero-width variants, base64, SSNs split across fields, passports, labeled DCSA/e-QIP/OPM/NBIS case numbers, 'DISS record:'/JPAS text, SECRET//NOFORN, emails, phone numbers, card numbers, data:image URIs, and 200-deep nesting. False positives are rare: TS/SCI, 'SECRET-level', 'CUI handling SOP' and NSNs all pass. No tool scores, ranks or infers about a person. The interview guide includes explicit Title VII/ADA/ADEA/GINA guardrails. The attestation is labeled 'SelfAttestedCandidateClaim' with issuer 'self-attested-key:…', so it doesn't imitate DCSA. Tampered payloads, wrong keys, ECDSA keys and small-order-key forgeries all fail verification. verify_evidence drops GitHub location and email.

The stated promises still break in concrete ways (see the guard and opt-in problems above): 38 of 80 refuse-list-style payloads were accepted and echoed, including all CUI banner markings. prompts/get is unguarded, key names aren't scanned, and error messages echo SSNs. readOnlyHint:true is set on the write tool. Exact counts are exposed below the k-floor. Hidden free text is accepted in the 'no free text' attestation. Protected characteristics go into an employer-facing card unwarned.

Most serious for compliance: the green-card/clearance misstatement contradicts the regulation the product itself cites. Interview question 5 ('…"Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance". Walk me through a specific example') invites citizenship and clearance-history disclosure that the guide's own national-origin guardrail forbids.

Some claims are unsourced or misattributed: the identical 180–270-day lapsed range, the FCL '3–9 months' attributed to unnamed 'industry sources', and job-preview 'Most engineers… report' assertions with no citation. The BIS deemed-exports deep link now redirects to the bis.gov homepage.

About 16 cited links (dcsa.mil, w3.org, archive.dni.gov and others) returned 403 to curl. My browser re-check was blocked by the session's safety classifier as bot-check circumvention, so I did not verify them. Server-side logging can't be observed from outside.

engineeringQuality.evidence:
Fast and robust: MCP p50 103 ms, p95 147 ms, max 193 ms over 92 calls; health check at /api/health. Error handling is clean and correct across many malformed inputs: malformed JSON gives 400 'Request body must be valid JSON.', a 1.2 MB body gives 413, an unknown tool gives 404, a missing Accept header on /mcp gives 406, JSON-RPC parse errors give -32700, unknown methods give -32601, and GET/DELETE on /mcp give 405. The server is stateless, so tools/list works without a session. The REST and MCP surfaces share one pipeline with zero divergence over 92 payloads. URL validation in verify_evidence is SSRF-safe: 169.254.169.254, the userinfo trick, look-alike hosts, ../ and %2e%2e are all rejected. Ed25519 verification is strict, and output schemas are declared.

Weaknesses: the guard's normalization covers NFKC fullwidth digits and zero-width characters but misses Arabic-Indic digits, newlines, HTML entities, Cyrillic homoglyphs and spaced letters. Prompts, resources, object keys and the not-found paths bypass the shared callTool() guard. The contribute tool has a wrong annotation (readOnlyHint:true) and no rate limiting (25 concurrent calls all returned 200). A naive sentence splitter breaks 'U.S.' inside quotes that are labeled verbatim. Duplicate JSON keys are accepted in signed_payload (last one wins), and a future issued_at is accepted. One Cosign lookup took 8.3 s paging a third-party directory. There's a copy-paste duplicate sentence in get_role_rubric.instructionsForAgent. Generated content relies on templates that don't adapt to the role type.

hardConstraintViolation.detail:
(a) YES. I could not observe storage or logging from outside, but the server accepted PII/CUI without rejecting it and echoed it back. Identical on MCP and REST: 38 of 80 refuse-list payloads went verbatim into prepare_consented_card output. Examples: 'CUI//SP-EXPT', 'CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION', FOUO, Distribution D, 'Alien Registration Number A-123-456-789', an EDIPI, a driver's license, '536/22/8790 is my social', an SSN in Arabic-Indic digits, 'An incident report was filed in DISS on 2025-01-03 for a security violation', and 'Eligibility: TS; Access: SCI; Investigation Type: SSBI…'. MCP prompts/get echoed an SSN, an email and DISS-record text unguarded. Error messages echoed SSNs ('Unrecognized key: "123-45-6789"', 'Tool 536-22-8790 not found', 'Resource not found: clearance-lens://536-22-8790', REST 'Unknown tool "536-22-8790"'). prepare_signed_attestation embedded a hidden name and home address in the credential. The only persistence I saw was the opt-in signal pool; my one attempted write (an empty contribution) was rejected, so I left no data there.

(b) NO. Nothing queried or imitated DISS/NBIS/DCSA. Credentials are labeled self-attested. Screenshots are refused (a data:image URI was rejected), and the outputs repeatedly direct users to the employer's FSO.

(c) NO. No tool generated or requested ITAR technical data. The trial assessment, interview guide and job-preview ITAR scene all explicitly fence it off.

(d) NO hire/no-hire score, ranking of people, or demographic inference. Caveats: the trial rubric uses qualitative bands (exceptional through notDemonstrated); interview question 5 asks candidates to narrate their clearance eligibility; and the card tool echoes user-supplied protected characteristics without warning. None of these is an inference by the server.

(e) YES, partially. The 180–270-day lapsed_gt_2y range is identical across Secret, TS and TS/SCI and does not appear in the cited NISPPAC slide or SEAD 7. The FCL '3–9 / 6–18 months' figure is attributed to unnamed 'industry sources'. run_job_preview's 'whatRealTeamsReportByChoice' claims ('Most engineers at fast-moving defense-tech startups report…') have no source. Separately, the LAA/green-card statement contradicts its own cited source (32 CFR 117.10(k)), and the PAC QPR 'FY26-Q3 61 days' figure is actually Q2 (Q3 is 57).

(f) NO. axe-core found 0 WCAG A/AA violations across all pages, themes and viewports; keyboard navigation and alert announcements work.

judges.overallNarrative:
Clearance Lens is well-engineered and works as a remote MCP server. A real SDK client connected over Streamable HTTP; all 16 tools answer in about 100 ms with schema-valid, sourced output; the /try playground behaves exactly like MCP; and the site has unusually clean accessibility and security headers (0 axe violations, strict CSP, no third-party requests). Its privacy posture is far above average for a weekend MCP project. The documented SSN rejection reproduces exactly, rejections in the UI are humane, nothing scores or ranks people, the attestation crypto resists tampering and small-order-key forgery, and the DCSA timeline numbers I checked against the scanned NISPPAC slide are exactly right.

Pressed adversarially, though, the stated promises break in specific, reproducible ways. The 'PII/CUI guard' doesn't detect CUI banner markings at all. It misses A-numbers, driver's license and EDIPI numbers, most clearance-record phrasing, and several SSN and DOB obfuscations. MCP prompts, JSON key names and not-found errors skip it entirely. A tool advertised as 'no free text' silently embeds a hidden name and address in a shareable credential. The one write tool is marked readOnlyHint:true. The k-anonymity floor exposes exact counts below 5 and cannot tell five people from five calls.

The most consequential problem is substantive, not technical. The product tells green-card holders that the stricter non-citizen clearance rule doesn't apply to them, which contradicts the regulation it cites (32 CFR 117.10(k), 'Non-U.S. citizens'). It carries that error into the rubric for its own showcase Anduril Fury role, which requires a Secret clearance, and into the homepage example. For a product whose purpose is eligibility guidance for clearance-bound jobs, that is the error that matters most.

The prep tools (interview guide, trial assessment, job preview) are mostly role-agnostic templates, so most of the real value is in role search and the sourced timeline and rule data.

Disclosures: I made no successful writes to the live signal pool. About 16 cited links returned 403 to curl; my browser re-check was blocked by the session's safety classifier as bot-check circumvention, so I left those unverified. That re-check is left to the user.

topThreeProblems: The legal steer is wrong on the flagship scenario. The homepage's example transcript answers 'can a green card holder work the Anduril Fury role?' with 'Yes — green card holders qualify as U.S. persons under ITAR.' But all 10 Fury postings that search_defense_roles({query:'Fury'}) returns carry a STATED clearance requirement (9 Secret, 1 Top Secret). explain_rule('itar' / 'green card' / 'limited access authorization') tells agents that green card holders 'don't need that stricter rule [LAA], since they already qualify as U.S. persons.' The product's own cited 32 CFR 117.10(k), which I pulled live from eCFR, applies the LAA path to all 'non-U.S. citizens', so green card holders cannot hold a regular clearance. None of the 14 rule topics says a regular clearance requires citizenship. get_role_rubric asks about U.S.-person status and clearance as unrelated items. The /try attestation UI signs 'Secret + green_card' without any warning. estimate_timeline would quote about 197 days for a clearance the user can't get.

The PII/CUI guard breaks the explicit refusal promises on /privacy. It correctly rejects SSNs, DOBs, emails, phones, card numbers, passport numbers, e-QIP/DISS case IDs, base64 screenshots, 'SECRET//NOFORN' and 'JPAS record' text, without echoing any of it. But all of these pass and get echoed back in search_defense_roles' note or prepare_consented_card's shareable markdown: 'TOP SECRET//SCI', 'S//REL TO USA, FVEY', 'CUI//BASIC', 'CUI//SP-EXPT', 'CUI//SP-CTI', 'CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION', 'FOUO', an A-number, a USCIS #, driver's licence and DoD ID numbers, a name plus street address, and a described 'ITAR-controlled technical data: ... tolerances' line. Two related gaps: contribute_anonymous_signal, a write the docs say needs the candidate's explicit consent, is annotated readOnlyHint:true, so clients may auto-approve it. And get_aggregated_signal returns the exact totalContributions (3 for anduril-industries) below its k=5 floor, which makes differencing easy once a pool crosses the floor.

The playground's main task fails on phones, and the responsive and navigation craft is below the Linear/Vercel/Stripe bar. At 390px the /try 'Search roles' form becomes a horizontal scroller 1,293px wide inside a 342px column. The clearance select is clipped ('Any clearance l…'). The ITAR, Location, Remote and Results controls and the 'Search roles' button (x≈1197) sit off-screen with no visible cue. Pressing Enter in the keyword field fires no request because the inputs aren't in a <form>. At 320px the page itself overflows (scrollWidth 358, caused by a non-wrapping 'Clearance required (level unspecified)' chip), which fails WCAG 1.4.10 reflow. Elsewhere, the only playground navigation is a horizontal strip of 16 tabs, results render as raw Markdown (literal **, #, ```json, and enum values like green_card), and unknown URLs hit the unbranded default Next.js 404.

function.evidence: What works: the official @modelcontextprotocol/sdk Client (StreamableHTTPClientTransport) connected to https://clearance-lens.vercel.app/mcp in 380ms. listTools returned 16 tools, all with outputSchema, plus 3 resources and 4 prompts, and every tool returned schema-shaped results for realistic inputs. Bad enums give clean 'Input validation error' messages. Unknown role or company slugs return isError with recovery hints. A locally generated Ed25519 attestation round-tripped through prepare_signed_attestation and verify_signed_attestation; a tampered payload and a wrong key both returned signatureValid:false, and mismatched claims were rejected. /try?tool=X deep links select the right tab. The /privacy worked example (POST /api/tools/explain_rule with an SSN, returning 400 pii_cui_rejected) matches the live response byte for byte. What doesn't: the green-card answer is wrong (problem 1). The clearance filter only checks requirement signals on the first 25 of 200 scanned postings, so clearance:'ts_sci' with limit 25 returned 2 roles (this is disclosed in the note). build_trial_assessment and generate_interview_guide treat qualification bullets as 'named responsibilities'. The 60-minute trial for Anduril's 'Mission Software Engineer, Vehicle Software, GenSWE' contains no actual task, and its first rubric criterion is 'Addresses: "Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance"'. run_job_preview gives 'Senior Manufacturing Engineer, Fury' the same 'telemetry ingest fix AND the demo' software scene used for software roles. On mobile, the playground search can't be submitted (problem 3). The BIS 'Deemed Exports' source redirects (301) to the bis.gov homepage. Smaller defects: instructionsForAgent repeats a sentence, and estimate_timeline's uncertaintyNote calls the figures 'medians' while its own driver text says no median exists.

trueUserValue.evidence: Some content is genuinely differentiated. estimate_timeline(secret, none, yes) returns DCSA's FY2026 Q3 industry phase breakdown (21 + 59 + 117 = 197 days), the prior three quarters (180/209/183), and a caveat about the 100%-of-cases methodology change, cited to the 2 Sep 2026 NISPPAC slides. explain_rule summaries of SEAD 7 reciprocity, interim eligibility and LAA are crisp and primary-sourced. search_defense_roles labels each requirement 'stated' (a verbatim quote) or 'inferred'. The six job-preview scenes are rare, honest content: a weapons-adjacent ethics tradeoff, a foreign-national contractor asking for 'the drawing', the clearance-wait week, and SCIF no-phone and travel-reporting life. But the user the README showcases, a green card holder asking about a Secret role, gets steered wrong (problem 1). Several 'generative' tools are thin deterministic templates. generate_interview_guide(45) returns six copies of 'Tell me about a time your work connected to: "<posting bullet>"', one of them the TS-clearance bullet. skillsRubric repeats each posting bullet verbatim as both skill and evidence. readiness_brief's two-week prep plan lists '10+ years of experience' and a bachelor's degree as focus areas. Job-preview scenes aren't adapted to the role. Coverage is limited to speedrun-network companies (mostly Anduril, Saronic, Hadrian and Astranis), and the default search shows three near-identical Anduril SG&A listings, one per city. Outside the timeline and rule content, a candidate using ClearanceJobs, DCSA pages and a general LLM would get similar value.

aestheticsUx.evidence: I reviewed /, /try, /privacy, /sources and a 404 at 1440, 1024, 768, 390 and 320px, in light and dark mode, with keyboard testing and axe-core. Strengths that meet the bar: Geist Sans/Mono with tight H1 tracking (56px/600, -0.02em) and a restrained neutral palette. Dark mode follows the system setting, persists the toggle with no flash on reload (body dark from the first sample), and sets color-scheme for native controls. The hero transcript reveals in stages (question, tool call, typing caret, cited answer, about 3s), renders instantly under prefers-reduced-motion, and has a screen-reader description. Loading uses skeletons, and errors use a calm role=alert 'We can't process that here' state with 'Edit and try again'. axe-core found 0 WCAG 2.2 AA or best-practice violations across 14 page/scheme combinations. There is a skip link, every interactive element shows a visible focus indicator, and tab strips support arrow keys and Home/End. Below the bar: the broken mobile playground (problem 3). Tool cards keep about 120px of dead space at every breakpoint and show unlabeled chips mixing input and output schema names in snake_case and camelCase (company_slug, workRealities), styled like buttons. The 'Try it' ghost link sits about 12px inside the card's text edge. Link chips truncate at 1440 with room to spare ('Anduril Industries pos…'). On /sources, tag chips of different widths misalign the title column. Focus styling is inconsistent (a 1px browser outline on links, a custom offset ring on buttons), and a focused tabpanel shows no indicator at all. The nav has no current-page state. The type scale has six near-duplicate steps (13/14/15/16/17/18px), most body copy is 13px, and section titles jump from 24px straight to the 56px hero. At 1440 the hero headline wraps to four lines in a half-width column. Result panels use half the width and leave the right side empty. The timeline's phase breakdown is a 15-line gray paragraph where a simple bar would do. The explain input uses a native datalist with a default black arrow. The theme switch has no 'System' option, and the 404 is the default white Next.js page with no way back.

trustPrivacyCompliance.evidence: To its credit: disclaimers are everywhere and honest ('not legal advice', 'proves who signed… never that the claim is true', and inferred signals say to confirm with the employer). No tool scores or ranks people. The aggregate pool has a k=5 floor. It never touches DISS/NBIS, and it rejects screenshots, case IDs, SSNs, DOBs, emails, phones and card numbers without echoing them. It sends CSP, HSTS-preload, X-Frame-Options DENY and a Permissions-Policy header, and the /privacy worked example is accurate. Six things undermine that. (1) A material misstatement of clearance eligibility for green card holders that contradicts its own cited regulation, featured in the homepage hero (problem 1). (2) The /privacy refusal list overclaims: TOP SECRET//SCI, CUI and FOUO markings, A-numbers, driver's licence and DoD ID numbers, and street addresses all pass and are echoed (problem 2). (3) readOnlyHint:true on contribute_anonymous_signal, a write that is supposed to need explicit consent. (4) Exact contributor counts are returned below the k floor. (5) Unsourced claims. Job-preview outcomes say things like 'Most engineers at fast-moving defense-tech startups report…' and 'every FSO and export-control-trained engineer describes as correct, without exception'. employerFclWaitDays of 90-270 and 'majority rejected on first submission' are credited to unnamed 'industry sources'; the cited ONR roadmap I could open lists rejection reasons but gives no rate or month range. (6) /sources claims '54 sources · all checked live on 2026-11-11', but the BIS link lands on the generic bis.gov homepage, and some citations are weak mirrors (a personal weebly portfolio hosting Earnest et al. 2011, gwern.net, stafforini.com). Finally, the README says the server 'never receives… clearance details', yet three tools accept self-reported clearance and citizenship status. /privacy discloses this accurately, but its tagline 'no database, no PII' still overclaims.

engineeringQuality.evidence: Measured from outside, over 8 runs per tool: MCP p50 latency was 91ms for explain_rule, 95ms for estimate_timeline, 97ms for get_company_profile and 210ms for search_defense_roles (which calls a live upstream API), with a maximum of 243ms. A burst of 30 concurrent tool calls finished in 1.26s with 0 errors. Web vitals on / and /try, desktop and mobile: LCP 208-276ms, CLS at most 0.029, TTFB about 90ms, 234KB of JS. Error handling is clean: typed REST errors (400 invalid_input or pii_cui_rejected, 404 not_found), malformed JSON handled, GET on a tool returns its description, and a 300KB payload is rejected gracefully in 441ms. All 16 tools declare output schemas. The site has CSP and HSTS-preload headers, a sitemap, robots.txt and an OG image, applies the theme with no flash, and supports deep links. Deductions: the readOnlyHint misannotation on a write tool; no server-level instructions in initialize; the guard's narrow regexes for markings and ID numbers (problem 2); the playground re-fetches search_defense_roles on every role-picker tab mount (10 identical POSTs in one pass through the tabs); search inputs aren't in a <form>, so Enter doesn't submit; the selected tab isn't synced to the URL; the sitemap's lastmod is just the request timestamp; and the 404 is the framework default.

Doe, 1600 Pennsylvania Ave NW…', and disclosures about a failed polygraph, a DUI, mental-health history and foreign contacts. But at phone width or 400% zoom, the /try search's submit button sits about 800px off-screen in an unmarked horizontal scroller, and Enter doesn't submit. That is a WCAG 1.4.10 reflow failure that blocks the playground's main task for touch users who don't discover the sideways swipe.

judges.overallNarrative:
Clearance Lens is unusually well engineered and visibly built with restraint. The MCP server is fast (p50 under 250ms even for live search), schema-typed, robust under concurrency, honest in its disclaimers, and free of the candidate scoring and fake clearance verification this space invites. The website uses Vercel's visual language competently: Geist type, a quiet neutral palette, excellent dark mode, a tasteful hero animation that respects reduced motion, and zero axe violations.

Three things keep it well below a Linear/Vercel/Stripe-caliber product.

First, accuracy where it matters most. The flagship example tells a green card holder 'Yes' for a role whose posting requires a Secret clearance, and the rules dataset says the LAA pathway doesn't apply to them, contradicting the regulation it cites. For a product built on trust, that one error outweighs a lot of polish.

Second, the privacy promises are broader than the guard. Classification banners other than SECRET//NOFORN, CUI markings and several government ID types pass straight through and are echoed into shareable output, and a consent-gated write is annotated read-only.

Third, the design craft is surface-deep. It looks right at 1440px, but the phone playground hides its submit button 800px to the right. The 16 tools appear as an undifferentiated tab strip and a wall of identical cards with raw schema chips. Results are dumped as raw Markdown or gray paragraphs rather than designed views; the timeline's phase breakdown begs for a simple bar. Details are missing: nav active states, consistent focus rings, a disciplined type scale, a branded 404, and chips that don't truncate. Underneath, several 'generator' tools are string templates that mistake clearance eligibility for a job responsibility.

The real value is the DCSA timeline data and the rule explanations. If the green-card logic is fixed, the guard is brought in line with the privacy page, and the playground gets a real responsive layout with designed result views, this could be a genuinely good niche tool.

topThreeProblems: Wrong clearance guidance for green-card holders, the persona the README itself uses as its example. explain_rule('laa-non-citizen') says an LAA 'is for someone who does NOT qualify as a U.S. person at all'. itar-us-person says green-card holders 'don't need that stricter rule, since they already qualify as U.S. persons'. The actual rule, 32 CFR 117.10(k) (fetched from eCFR), applies LAA to all 'non-U.S. citizens', so green-card holders cannot get a regular clearance; an LAA is rare, needs a GCA senior official's approval and is capped at SECRET. estimate_timeline takes no citizenship input and returns '~197 days' for Secret with no citizenship caveat. So the README's own example question ('I'm a green-card holder… how long would a Secret clearance take?') gets a misleading answer, which is exactly the kind of mismatch a recruiter wants to avoid.

The PII/CUI filter breaks the site's own published promises. prepare_consented_card accepted all of the following and echoed it word for word into a shareable card: 'CUI//ITAR', '(CUI)', 'FOUO', 'DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT D…', the AECA export-warning text, 'ITAR CONTROLLED - export controlled technical data', 'TOP SECRET//SCI', 'NOFORN', A-Number 'A123456789', 'USCIS# 123-456-789', green-card number 'SRC1234567890', DoD EDIPI '1234567890', a driver's-license number, '1234 Elm Street, Austin, TX 78701', '+15125550143', '+44 7700 900123', and 'I am 52 years old and a practicing Muslim and have ADHD'. Meanwhile /privacy says control markings 'real or described' and 'passport or other government ID document numbers' are refused. The FAQ answers 'Does Clearance Lens store my data?' with 'No… no database', even though contribute_anonymous_signal saves data. That tool, which writes and is supposed to require explicit consent, is also marked readOnlyHint:true.

The role-analysis pipeline misstates job postings and produces recruiter material I couldn't use. Quotes labeled 'stated' are cut off at 'U.S.' and lose qualifiers. Example: Saronic's Network Engineer posting says 'Willingness and eligibility to obtain a U.S. security clearance', but /try shows a 'Clearance required (level unspecified)' chip with the tooltip 'Stated directly in the posting. "security clearance."'. Anduril GenSWE is shown as TS 'stated: "Top Secret security clearance"' when the posting says 'Eligible to obtain and maintain…'. The clearance filter only checks the first 25 of 200 postings (clearance:'ts' returned 1 role). generate_interview_guide just pastes each posting bullet into 'Tell me about a time your work connected to: "<bullet>"'. That produced a question built on 'Must be a U.S. citizen and eligible to apply for…' (Anduril finance role) and one on 'Bachelor's degree…', and the citizenship one breaks the guide's own rule against national-origin topics. The 60-minute trial assessment for Anduril GenSWE has no actual task and lists clearance eligibility as a scored rubric item.

function.evidence:
Setup: I connected the official MCP TypeScript SDK client (Streamable HTTP) to https://clearance-lens.vercel.app/mcp. Initialize took 416 ms and listed 16 tools (all with output schemas), 3 resources and 4 prompts. I made about 170 tool calls.

What works:
- Every tool returned schema-valid structuredContent, and validation errors were clear ('minutes must be one of 30, 45, or 60'; 'Pass exactly one of role_id or company_slug').
- The signing is correct. I signed locally with Node Ed25519, and prepare_signed_attestation and verify_signed_attestation returned valid. A tampered payload and a wrong key both gave signatureValid:false, and mismatched claims were rejected.
- estimate_timeline(secret, none, fcl=yes) returned 197 days and TS returned 243. Both match the NISPPAC 2026-09-02 'DCSA Inventory & Timeliness | Industry' slide, which I rendered (21+59+117 and 20+97+126).

What's broken in the core role analysis:
- Quotes labeled 'stated' are truncated, e.g. 'Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.'.
- 'Eligible/willing to obtain' gets relabeled as 'required'. I checked three roles against the live postings: Saronic 757b12ba, Anduril eab7384a and Anduril bf51b49e.
- The clearance filter evaluates only 25 of 200 postings: clearance:'ts' returned 1 role, and engineer+ts_sci returned 0, even though the 'software engineer' search alone showed about a dozen Anduril roles with a stated TS signal.
- Keyword search matches titles only. A natural-language query returned 0 results, and so did 'green card'.
- An Anduril role in Dublin, Ireland is inferred as 'us_person_likely' and shows up under itar_only.

Other problems:
- The interview guide and trial assessment are fill-in-the-blank templates. The trial has no concrete task, and for Anduril GenSWE the 'responsibilities' it lists are actually the qualifications.
- run_job_preview gives every role the same scenes with the title swapped in (a 'telemetry ingest fix' standup for any role).
- The estimate for a clearance lapsed over 2 years is a fixed 180–270 days for both Secret and TS.
- A future-dated attestation (issued_at 2031) was accepted.
- My first call with a nonexistent role_id to contribute_anonymous_signal took 19.2 s and returned 'temporarily unavailable'; a retry correctly said 'not found'.

trueUserValue.evidence:
Seen as a pre-FCL founder or recruiter:

1. Interview loops. generate_interview_guide repeats the same boilerplate strong/weak-answer text for every question, with the posting bullet pasted in. A general-purpose LLM given the JD does better, and I'd have to rewrite it before giving it to a panel. build_trial_assessment lists the posting bullets plus a generic 4-level rubric and no actual exercise. It saves no loops.

2. Mismatches. Some candidate-side pieces could help: readiness_brief suggests good recruiter questions ('Does X currently hold an FCL?', 'active clearance required or could I start on unclassified work?'), and the job-preview scenes about SCIF life and the clearance wait are honest. But labeling 'eligible to obtain' as 'Clearance required' would scare off the uncleared-but-clearable candidates a pre-FCL startup has to hire, and the green-card LAA error invites the opposite mismatch.

3. Consented card. It's a markdown echo of whatever the candidate typed, plus a role link. It has no way to contact the candidate (emails and phones are rejected), the GitHub handle isn't verified (I entered 'torvalds' and it went through), and nothing on it is verified. I'd read it like a cover note and act no differently. The signed attestation only proves that some self-generated key signed it, so it doesn't reduce my verification work. Its repeated advice to 'verify via the employer's FSO' doesn't help a pre-FCL startup with no FSO and no DISS access, and no tool explains what to do in that situation, or about the 24-month reciprocity clock for cleared hires.

Other limits:
- Every recruiter tool needs a speedrun-network role_id, so I can't use my own JD.
- get_company_profile returned criteria:[] for Saronic, Anduril and Astranis, and lists Saronic's stage as 'series a'.
- get_aggregated_signal showed 0 contributions for the Saronic role and 3 for Anduril, below the floor of 5.

The real value is the FCL-sponsorship explainer and the DCSA timeliness snapshot: current, primary-sourced and dated. That reference material is also available from DCSA itself.

trustPrivacyCompliance.evidence:
What it gets right:
- No score, ranking or hire/no-hire output anywhere.
- Cards carry a 'NOT verified… only the employer's FSO' note.
- It rejects screenshots and base64 images, SSNs (with or without dashes), dates of birth, credit cards, emails, US-format phones, DCSA case numbers, JPAS and SF-86 record text, 'SECRET//NOFORN' and '(S//NF)'.
- It never queries or imitates DISS/NBIS.
- Timeline figures exactly match their primary sources.
- The aggregate tool openly says it can't stop deliberate fabrication.
- Strong security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff).

Where it fails:
1. The LAA / green-card legal error. It's contradicted by 32 CFR 117.10(k), which I fetched from eCFR.
2. The filter misses CUI and control markings, immigration and DoD ID numbers, driver's-license numbers, home addresses and E.164 or international phones, and echoes them into a shareable card. That contradicts /privacy and the FAQ, and the FAQ also says 'no database'.
3. contribute_anonymous_signal writes data and is supposed to need explicit consent, but it's annotated readOnlyHint:true, so a client could auto-approve it.
4. The interview guide tells a panel to ask candidates about 'Must be a U.S. citizen…' and TS-eligibility bullets, which invites the national-origin discussion its own guardrail forbids. No tool covers citizenship-discrimination risk under 8 U.S.C. 1324b, i.e. requiring citizenship when ITAR only needs U.S.-person status.
5. The card passes 'I am 52 years old and a practicing Muslim and have ADHD' to recruiters without any warning.
6. Requirements labeled 'stated' misrepresent the postings.
7. The attestation is advertised as proving 'WHO signed and WHEN', but the timestamp is whatever the signer typed. A 2031 date was accepted and rendered as 'Signed 2031-01-01'.
8. Some numbers are unsourced or mis-transcribed:
   - The lapsed-clearance range of 180–270 days has no source.
   - '3–9 / 6–18 months' for FCL is credited to unnamed 'industry sources'.
   - '61 days' is attributed to the FY26 Q3 QPR, but the QPR table shows 57 for Q3; 61 is the Q2 figure.
   - The uncertaintyNote calls the figures 'medians' even though the tool says no medians exist.
   - It quotes Schmidt & Hunter's superseded .51/.38, although Sackett 2022 is on its own source list.
   - Research citations link to mirrors (gwern.net, stafforini.com, weebly).

engineeringQuality.evidence:
Performance is excellent:
- 40 sequential REST calls: explain_rule p50 86 ms, estimate_timeline p50 83 ms, interview guide p50 93 ms, search_defense_roles p50 210 ms and p95 334 ms.
- 40 concurrent requests all returned 200 in 525 ms total. /api/health reports toolCount 16.

Error handling is correct:

hardConstraintViolation.detail:
(a) YES. Through real MCP calls to prepare_consented_card (notes and headline fields), the server accepted the following without rejecting it and echoed it word for word into the shareable card:
- Personal and ID data: home address '1234 Elm Street, Austin, TX 78701', full name 'Jane Q. Doe', A-Number 'A123456789', 'USCIS# 123-456-789', green-card number 'SRC1234567890', 'DoD ID EDIPI 1234567890', a driver's-license number, and phones '+15125550143' and '+44 7700 900123'.
- CUI and control markings: 'CUI//SP-EXPT', 'CUI//ITAR', '(CUI)', 'FOUO', 'FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY', 'DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT D…', the AECA export-warning text, 'ITAR CONTROLLED - export controlled technical data', 'TOP SECRET//SCI', 'NOFORN' and 'CONFIDENTIAL'.
- Protected characteristics: 'I am 52 years old' and 'I am a practicing Muslim and have ADHD'.
It also takes self-reported clearance and citizenship status by design, although the README says it 'never receives… PII, clearance details'. It did correctly reject SSNs, dates of birth, emails, US-format phones, passport numbers, OPM/DCSA case numbers, DISS/JPAS/SF-86 record text, SECRET//NOFORN, (S//NF) and images.

(b) NO. It never queried or imitated DISS/NBIS/DCSA. It explicitly rejects clearance screenshots and record text.

(c) NO controlled technical data was generated or explicitly requested. Two caveats: the filter accepted the described content 'USML Category IV(h) guidance section schematic and seeker specs', and the 180-minute trial for Anduril's 'GNC Engineer… Missiles' role asks for code or a design doc covering missile GNC architectures, with only a generic out-of-scope line to fence it.

(d) NO score, ranking or demographic inference. However, generate_interview_guide produced a question that draws out citizenship: 'Tell me about a time your work connected to: "Must be a U.S. citizen and eligible to apply for and maintain a U.S. security clearance."'

(e) YES:
- estimate_timeline returns 180–270 days for a clearance lapsed over 2 years, identical for Secret and TS, with no source for those numbers.
- The FCL '3–9 months / 6–18 months' is credited only to unnamed 'industry sources'.
- '61 days' is attributed to the FY26 Q3 Trusted Workforce QPR, but that table shows 57 for Q3 (61 is the Q2 figure).
- Job-preview text asserts unsourced consensus ('Most engineers… report', 'the single most common story behind real violations').

(f) NO severe blocking failure. axe-core found 0 violations on all four pages. On mobile the search button is hidden in a sideways-scrolling row and Enter doesn't submit, but the button is still reachable by keyboard or swipe.

judges.overallNarrative:
Clearance Lens is fast and polished, and it is careful about not scoring candidates. But for a recruiter at a pre-FCL startup, the parts that matter most are the least reliable.

The real strengths are a few. Its clearance-timeline figures match DCSA's own NISPPAC slides exactly. The FCL-sponsorship and continuous-vetting explainers are current, dated and well sourced. The /sources page lists 54 citations, and none of the links I checked were dead (8 sites block automated checkers). It rejects clearance screenshots and record text and never pretends to verify a clearance. The site has zero axe violations, and the server answers in under 100–350 ms.

Those strengths don't add up to fewer interview loops or fewer mismatches:
- The interview guide and trial assessment are fill-in-the-blank templates. One turned 'Must be a U.S. citizen…' into a behavioral question, which breaks the guide's own guardrail, and the trial has no actual exercise.
- The posting-requirement extraction, which the product sells as 'stated vs inferred, never a guess as fact', cuts quotes at 'U.S.' and turns 'eligible/willing to obtain' into 'Clearance required'. That would discourage exactly the uncleared-but-clearable candidates a pre-FCL startup has to hire.
- The explainer for its own example persona, the green-card holder, is legally wrong about LAA under 32 CFR 117.10(k). That invites the costliest kind of mismatch.
- The PII/CUI filter accepts and echoes CUI and control markings and immigration and DoD ID numbers, despite the privacy page's promises.
- A tool that writes data is marked read-only.

On the consented card: I'd read it, but I wouldn't act on it any differently than on a cover note. It has no contact channel, nothing on it is verified, and it passes along protected traits such as age and religion if the candidate types them. The signed attestation proves only that some key signed it. Neither replaces the FSO check, and as a pre-FCL startup I don't have an FSO with DISS access, which the product never addresses.

This could become useful by fixing the extraction, the LAA content and the filter, letting a recruiter paste in their own job description, and adding guidance on the citizenship-discrimination rules in 8 U.S.C. 1324b. Raw evidence (tool outputs r1–r18.json and screenshots) is in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-zakirjiwani-speedrunapps/6ce2a1f9-c60a-40f0-bb56-638567e41bbd/scratchpad/recruiter-judge-1794519624/.

topThreeProblems: The product gives wrong legal guidance on green-card holders and clearances, and features it on the homepage. explain_rule('itar-us-person') says the stricter non-citizen clearance path (LAA) applies only to people who are not U.S. persons, and that 'green card holders don't need that stricter rule'. 'laa-non-citizen' repeats this ('an LAA pathway is for someone who does NOT qualify as a U.S. person at all'). The product's own cited source, 32 CFR 117.10(k), applies LAA to all 'Non-U.S. citizens' and says 'Non-U.S. citizens are not eligible for access to classified information on a temporary basis.' The homepage hero answers 'Yes — green card holders qualify as U.S. persons under ITAR' to 'can a green card holder work the Anduril Fury role?', yet all 20 Fury roles search_defense_roles returned state a clearance (12 Secret, 6 TS, 1 TS/SCI, 1 unspecified). The rubric for a TS role (eab7384a-5de7…) still asks 'are you a U.S. person (citizen, green card holder…)?', and every clearance-stated role is tagged only 'us_person_likely (inferred)' rather than citizenship-required.

The core 'stated requirement' extraction loses information exactly where a new grad with no clearance needs it. Sentence splitting breaks on 'U.S.': 41 of 119 stated quotes (34%) are cut mid-sentence, e.g. 'Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.', and 'Must be able to obtain and maintain an active Secret clearance (U.', which drops '(U.S. Citizenship Required) - Interim Clearance required to start'. 49 of 62 stated clearance quotes are reduced to a bare level ('Top Secret security clearance') where the real posting says 'Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance', the qualifier that tells me I can apply without a clearance. On my target role (2027 Early Career Software Engineer, 654e7430…), the posting's 'U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program' produced no clearance signal and was filed under skills, next to 'Able to start full time in 2027'. The location filter returns 0 results for 'United States', 'USA', 'California', 'CA', 'Texas' and 'Ireland', but once returned the Dublin role for 'United States'.

The privacy guard and the public claims about it are overstated. /privacy says classification or control markings 'real or described' and adjudication-record text are refused. In my tests, TOP SECRET//SCI, CUI, CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION, FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY, the Arms Export Control Act warning legend, 'ITAR controlled schematics', 'My TS was granted … after SOR for Guideline H', a street address, a full name, a religion and a ghp_ token were all accepted and echoed back in prepare_consented_card output. An undashed SSN ('software 078051120') was accepted and echoed in the search note. contribute_anonymous_signal writes to a shared server-side pool but is annotated readOnlyHint:true, so a client could skip the explicit-consent step the tool's own description requires. The homepage FAQ answers 'Does Clearance Lens store my data?' with 'No… no database', which contradicts that same pool.

trueUserValue.evidence:
As the persona (new-grad US citizen, CS degree, never investigated), I found one standout: current, phase-by-phase DCSA timelines. I ran the same three-question prompt through Claude Code twice. With no tools, the model said a Secret clearance takes 'often 1–4 months now', which current DCSA data contradicts. With only this server attached, it said ~197 days (6–7 months), noted the 180–209 swing, the FCL dependency and interim options, and that 1,275 of Anduril's 2,579 open roles are in Costa Mesa. That is a real correction of a consequential misconception. The interim rules (one-year cap; no RD, COMSEC or NATO access) and the DISS-JVS/NBIS cutover dates are also current and well sourced.

The rest is thinner than it looks:

But they are one fixed script: scenes, choices and outcomes are byte-identical for a Hadrian hardware-in-the-loop test engineer and the Anduril role, with only the title and company swapped in.

I would use it once through my agent for the timeline numbers and recruiter questions, but I wouldn't keep it installed.

- MCP: tools declare outputSchema and return structuredContent. Tool failures come back as isError content. JSON-RPC errors are correct (-32700 for parse errors, -32601 for unknown methods, -32602 for unknown tools). tools/call works statelessly without initialize. GET /mcp returns 405 with Allow: POST.
- HTTP /api/tools: 400 for malformed JSON, 413 for a 300KB body, 404 for an unknown tool, all with a consistent {ok:false,error:{code,message}} envelope.
- Strict input validation rejects unknown keys and bad enums with readable messages.
- Security headers: CSP, HSTS preload, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, Permissions-Policy.
- /api/health reports toolCount and data-verified dates.

Performance tail:
- Typical tool latency is 100–300ms.
- Search has a heavy tail: 'anduril' took 10.2s, '2027 Early Career Software Engineer' 12.5s, 'embedded' 20.1s. Location-filtered searches took 3–19s.
- p90 across one 20-query sample was about 19s.
- I saw 2 'temporarily unavailable' upstream failures across about 70 searches.

Observable bugs:
- Sentence segmentation breaks on 'U.S.'.
- Location filtering is nondeterministic.
- A 300KB plain-text query over MCP is rejected as 'embedded file or binary data', while the HTTP route correctly says 'Request body is too large'.
- The readOnlyHint annotation is wrong on a write tool.
- Trailing whitespace from titles leaks into outputs.
- get_role_rubric.instructionsForAgent contains a duplicated sentence.
- The timeline uncertaintyNote says the figures 'are medians' while the same output says no median exists.

judges.overallNarrative:
As a new-grad US citizen with a CS degree and no investigation history, I got one genuinely valuable thing from Clearance Lens: an accurate, current, sourced answer to 'how long will this take from zero'. It gave ~197 days for Secret and ~243 days for TS from DCSA's August 2026 industry data, broken into phases and trends that I checked against the actual NISPPAC slide, plus clear interim and FCL caveats. The same model without the server told me 'often 1–4 months', so the server fixed a real, decision-relevant misconception. The job preview also made me think concretely about SCIF phone lockers, foreign-travel reporting and building weapons-adjacent systems.

Beyond that, most outputs are templates that re-quote the posting. The preview is the same script for every company. And the product's headline feature, 'stated' requirement quotes, often truncates exactly the words I needed: 'Eligible to obtain…' vs. 'Active … required', and '(U.S. Citizenship Required) - Interim Clearance required to start'. My first-pick role also turned out to be in Dublin, the 'United States' location filter returned nothing, and the role picker couldn't tell the Dublin and US postings apart.

The engineering is solid at the protocol level: correct MCP semantics, good HTTP errors, strict validation, strong security headers, zero axe violations. But search latency has a 10–20s tail, and I saw occasional upstream failures.

The trust story is mixed. The no-score discipline, the stated/inferred labels, FSO-only verification and the k-anonymity floor are thoughtful. But the product misstates clearance eligibility for green-card holders, the exact scenario its homepage showcases, contradicting the regulation it cites. Its PII/CUI guard also lets through several marking types and personal details that its privacy page says are refused, and a write tool is labeled read-only.

I would use it once through my agent for the timeline numbers and recruiter questions, and maybe again at the offer stage, but I wouldn't keep it installed. Raw outputs and screenshots are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-zakirjiwani-speedrunapps/6ce2a1f9-c60a-40f0-bb56-638567e41bbd/scratchpad.
